title: 8 Ju Ji-hoon K-dramas to revisit during “The Remarried Empress” - Hashtag Legend Hong Kong

 By Tom Kao November 12, 2026 Twenty years after making his acting breakthrough as a crown prince in "Princess Hours," Ju Ji-hoon is back in royal robes for "The Remarried Empress. This time, he plays Emperor Sovieshu, whose decision to divorce Empress Navier (Shin Min-a) after falling for another woman sets the fantasy romance into motion. But royalty is only one side of Ju's acting career. From fighting zombies and solving mysteries to playing a charming lawyer and a brilliant trauma surgeon, here are eight Ju Ji-hoon K-dramas worth revisiting while watching "The Remarried Empress" 
 Princess Hours (2006)
 Photo: MBC
 The drama that started it all, Princess Hours introduced Ju Ji-hoon as Crown Prince Lee Shin in a fictional modern-day Korea where the monarchy still exists. His royal life takes an unexpected turn when he's pushed into an arranged marriage with ordinary high school student Shin Chae-kyeong (Yoon Eun-hye), thanks to an old promise between their grandfathers. Despite their clashing personalities and Shin's feelings for another girl, the two slowly grow closer while dealing with palace politics and a complicated love triangle. Twenty years later, it's a particularly fitting drama to revisit.
 Kingdom (2019-2020)
 Ju Ji-hoon returned to royal territory in Kingdom , although this time, romance was the least of his worries. Set during the Joseon dynasty, the historical zombie thriller follows Crown Prince Lee Chang as he investigates his father's mysterious illness, only to discover a deadly epidemic turning people into flesh-eating monsters. To make matters worse, a powerful political clan is plotting to take his place on the throne. Forced to flee the palace, Lee Chang finds himself fighting both the undead and his political enemies in a desperate attempt to save his kingdom.
 The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call (2025)
 One of Ju Ji-hoon's biggest recent hits, The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call sees him playing Baek Kang-hyuk, a brilliant but notoriously blunt surgeon who joins a struggling university hospital. Having spent years treating patients in war zones, he's determined to turn its neglected trauma unit into a life-saving team. Together with young doctor Yang Jae-won (Choo Young-woo) and nurse Cheon Jang-mi (Ha Young), he tackles one emergency after another while constantly clashing with hospital management. Ju's commanding performance even earned him Best Actor at the 2025 Baeksang Arts Awards.
 Also see: 5 things to know about Ju Ji-hoon, the star of “The Remarried Empress” 
 Hyena (2020)
 Swapping royal robes for tailored suits, Ju Ji-hoon plays ambitious lawyer Yoon Hee-jae in Hyena . Coming from a prestigious legal family, he's used to getting his way until he meets Jung Geum-ja (Kim Hye-soo), a fiercely competitive lawyer who tricks him into a romantic relationship to gain an advantage in court. Things get even messier when they end up working at the same law firm, handling cases for some of Korea's wealthiest clients. Between the sharp dialogue, constant mind games and undeniable chemistry, this is Ju at his most charismatic.
 Love Your Enemy (2024)
 For something a little lighter, Love Your Enemy brings Ju Ji-hoon back to romantic comedy territory. He plays Seok Ji-won, who unexpectedly reunites with his former teenage love and longtime rival Yoon Ji-won (Jung Yu-mi) after 18 years apart. Born on the same day into families that have feuded for generations, the two once shared a secret romance that ended in heartbreak. Now, Seok returns as chairman of their old high school, where Yoon works as a teacher, and it doesn't take long for their old rivalry and lingering feelings to resurface.
 Blood Free (2024)
 In the sci-fi thriller Blood Free , Ju Ji-hoon plays Woo Chae-woon, a former military officer who becomes the personal bodyguard of Yoon Ja-yu (Han Hyo-joo), the CEO of a biotechnology company revolutionising the food industry with artificially cultured meat. But he's not simply there to protect her. Chae-woon is secretly investigating a past terrorist attack that he suspects may be connected to her company. As Ja-yu faces growing threats from powerful rivals and mysterious hackers, the two find themselves caught up in a dangerous web of corporate conspiracies and political secrets.
 Jirisan (2021)
 Set against the breathtaking scenery of Mount Jiri, Jirisan follows a team of national park rangers tasked with rescuing hikers and keeping visitors safe. Ju Ji-hoon plays Kang Hyun-jo, a former army captain turned rookie ranger who begins experiencing mysterious visions of deaths occurring on the mountain. He soon teams up with experienced ranger Seo Yi-kang (Jun Ji-hyun), using his unusual ability to help locate missing hikers and investigate suspicious incidents. But as more unexplained deaths emerge, the pair begin to realise there may be something far more sinister happening on the mountain.
 Light Shop (2024)
 Taking a more mysterious turn, Light Shop follows a peculiar lighting store tucked away at the end of a dark alley, where strange customers arrive carrying secrets of their own. Ju Ji-hoon plays Jung Won-young, the enigmatic shop owner who seems to know more about his visitors than he lets on. As their seemingly unrelated stories begin to connect, the series gradually reveals the truth behind the shop and its connection to life and death. Blending supernatural horror with surprisingly emotional storytelling, it's a refreshing change from Ju's more outspoken characters.
